dedupe_keys.name: georeferenced dataset of maritime piracy in the gulf of guinea from 2010 to 2021

description: Georeferenced dataset of maritime piracy in the Gulf of Guinea from 2010 to 2021 is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Ricardo Moura et al. Piracy has been a global concern and a threat to the safety of people performing maritime trade around the globe. Since ancient times maritime piracy has been a common practice that, unfortunately, has not ended in the current days. Coverage: global; published in 2023. Formats: CSV, Excel, Pickle, Python. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
